title: A learning-evoked slow-oscillatory architecture paces population activity for offline reactivation across the human medial temporal lobe
title_zh: 学习诱发的慢振荡结构重塑人类内侧颞叶在脱离任务时的群体活动再激活节律
abstract: Memory processing requires coordinated engagement of neuronal populations across brain networks and over time. How such coordination is organized in the human medial temporal lobe (MTL) remains unclear. Here, we show that MTL population activity is dynamically structured by a transient slow-oscillatory architecture that emerges during learning to promote offline consolidation and later recall. Using intracranial recordings that combine single-neuron spiking activity and local field potentials in human participants, we find that mnemonic engagement elicits on-demand slow-oscillatory bursts in the hippocampus. These hippocampal bursts synchronize gamma-band patterns across MTL regions, defining discrete coordination events that pace cross-regional coactivity motifs during learning. These learning-evoked population motifs are selectively reactivated during hippocampal ripples in post-learning rest, and the strength of their reactivation predicts subsequent recall accuracy. Together, these findings identify a multi-scale coordination mechanism that links distributed population activity across learning, consolidation, and recall in humans.
abstract_zh: 记忆加工需要跨脑网络并跨时段协同地招募神经元群体。人类内侧颞叶（MTL）中这种协调如何组织仍不清楚。我们在此显示，MTL群体活动在学习过程中会被一种短暂出现的慢振荡结构动态塑形，该结构促进离线巩固和后续提取。通过结合人类受试者单细胞放电与局部场电位记录的颅内电生理数据，我们发现记忆参与可在海马中诱发按需的慢振荡爆发。这些海马慢振荡爆发可同步MTL各区的γ频段模式，定义离散的协同事件，从而在学习期间驱动跨区共活动模体。学习诱发的这些群体模体在学习后静息期的海马锐波涟漪中被选择性地再激活，再激活强度可预测后续提取准确性。总体而言，这些发现确定了一种多尺度协调机制，连接了人类学习、巩固与提取过程中的分布式群体活动。
